title: Context Grafting + KV Cache Trace Bindings
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Background: Many services observe increased tail latency when inference requests miss the prefix/KV cache. Current traces surface the end-to-end latency but do not reliably correlate cache hits/misses with individual spans because serverless frontends rehydrate contexts and middleware strip or mutate propagation headers.

Goal: Implement a minimal, low-overhead SDK/middleware change dubbed 'context grafting' that binds a stable tracing context to request-local KV cache metrics. This ticket implements the core SDK hooks and server middleware across Node and Go SDKs, instruments KV cache hits/misses as span attributes and structured events, and adds a lightweight reconciler to restore context across async boundaries (workers, queued jobs, and Lambda-style cold starts).

Non-goal: This ticket does not change sampling defaults or add long-term storage of per-request cache telemetry beyond span events; follow-ups will evaluate aggregation and retention policies.
acceptance_criteria: Node and Go SDKs expose a ContextGraft hook that can attach a stable span context to request metadata without forcing new sampling decisions

HTTP server middleware restores grafted context for inbound requests lacking an upstream trace header and emits a 'kv.cache' span event for each cache lookup (attributes: cache.key, result:{hit|miss}, latency_ms)
Worker/queue adapter rehydrates grafted context for background processing and links emitted spans to the original request span (via Link header) when applicable
E2E load test showing <2% added p95 latency overhead for instrumentation at 1000 RPS with realistic batch sizes
PRs merged: node-sdk#453, go-sdk#212, runtime-proxy#98 with integration tests and feature flags behind 'context_grafting'
tasks: Design: finalize propagation format (prefer graft-id + optional compact traceparent) and spec in Confluence
SDK: implement ContextGraft hook in node-sdk (fast path) and go-sdk (context.Context wrapper)
Middleware: add graft-aware middleware for express/grpc-go and http.Server
Runtime: emit kv.cache span events in the serving runtime when cache is consulted (C++ module change + thin binding)
Worker: add rehydration utility for queue consumers to link to original trace
Tests: unit + integration tests, synthetic perf harness, and fuzzer for header variations
Docs: public SDK docs and internal postmortem playbook entries
Dashboard: dashboard tile in Console for 'KV cache trace correlation' showing top endpoints by cache miss latency contribution
design_notes:
Propagation format: graft-id is a 16-byte hex token placed in header 'X-RW-GRAFT' and mapped to a lightweight span context in local process memory. If traceparent is present, graft attaches as Link to the existing span. For cold-start rehydration we persist graft-id in the request envelope and emit a synthetic 'graft.restore' event.

KV telemetry: runtime emits event 'kv.cache' with attributes cache.key, cache.bucket, result (hit|miss), latency_ms, and quantized_bucket for small cardinality. These events are attached to the active span and also exposed to telemetry exporter as line-delimited JSON to avoid schema churn.

Sampling: do not force sampling; graft does not alter sample decision. If the incoming request is unsampled but the graft hook is enabled, we still emit the kv.cache events as low-overhead events using the local transient buffer for sampled traces only. Follow-up will add adaptive sampling for cache-heavy endpoints.
